newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Client buys 14 pct of Burns Philp - DMG.
newsitem.headline: Client buys 14 pct of Burns Philp - DMG.

text.p: Broker Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said on Friday it had bought 78.16 million shares in spices and yeast group Burns Philp & Co Ltd at A$2.50 a share for a client that was not an international food group.
DMG director Robin Yandle told Reuters he would be active in the stock again later on Friday either as a buyer or a seller, depending on the price.
"We've bought 78.16 million shares or 14 percent of Burns Philp, all at A$2.50 a share, from a range of sellers, both domestic and international," Yandle said.
He said there had been 40 sellers and one buyer.
Yandle confirmed earlier comments to newspapers that the buyer was not an international food group and that he considered Goodman Fielder Ltd an international food group.
He said the client was an overseas based individual that does not have any food assets at this stage.
There has been some recent speculation that Goodman Fielder was considering a takeover bid for Burns Philp.
The offer price is 47 cents above Burns' A$2.03 closing price on Thursday.
The Sydney Morning Herald said Deutsche Morgan had acted for George Soros in the past.
The Australian Financial Review said some institutions believed the mystery buyer was a wealthy New Zealander, possibly Ron Brierley and his Guiness Peat Group Plc.
